theme_central: Ease or hardship do not measure a person's real honor in Allah's eyes — what counts is how he treats the orphan and the poor; closing on the tranquil soul invited to enter Paradise.
sources_note: Content widely taught and undisputed: the three destroyed peoples ('Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) and the final verse of the tranquil soul are classical landmarks.

branches.title: Oaths
branches.resume: Oath by the dawn, the ten nights, the even and the odd, the night as it passes.

children.t: Oaths by the dawn, the ten nights, the even and the odd

branches.title: The destroyed peoples
branches.resume: 'Ad of Iram with its pillars, Thamud who carved the rock, Pharaoh of the stakes: all committed excess.

children.t: 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh destroyed for their excess

branches.title: Ease and hardship
branches.resume: Man confuses divine honor with material ease, and disgrace with hardship — wrongly.

children.t: Ease or hardship do not measure real honor before Allah

branches.title: The orphan and the poor
branches.resume: Failure toward the orphan, indifference toward the poor, greed for inheritance and wealth.

children.t: Failure toward the orphan and the poor, material greed

branches.title: The tranquil soul
branches.resume: Earth crushed to powder, regret at not having done good; closing: "O tranquil soul, enter My Paradise".

children.t: Earth crushed to powder, regret at not having done good in life
"O tranquil soul, return well pleased and pleasing, enter My Paradise"
